variants.headline: A bargain with {{partner}}, and gold in the terms
body: We have struck terms with {{partner}}. Our side gives {{weGive}} and receives {{weGet}}, with gold among them.

variants.headline: A bargain abroad, with gold in the terms
body: Our envoys have struck terms with a foreign power, name unknown to the dispatches. Our side gives {{weGive}} and receives {{weGet}}, with gold among them.

variants.headline: The terms of the bargain
body: We give: {{weGive}}.
We receive: {{weGet}}.
Gold: counted among the terms.

variants.headline: Hear it! Terms are struck with {{partner}}
body: Mark it, good people, mark it: terms are struck with {{partner}}. We give {{weGive}}; we take {{weGet}}. Gold moves in the bargain, and the merchants will feel it first.

variants.headline: The envoys earn their keep
body: The envoys have settled terms with {{partner}}: we give {{weGive}}, we receive {{weGet}}. Making a bargain stick takes patience, and gold in the terms takes nerve. The paper calls that governing well.

variants.headline: A trade route bound for us is plundered
body: A trade route bound for our territory has been plundered on the road. The run is lost, and with it whatever our cities stood to draw from it.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} robs the road to our gates
body: {{plunderer}} has plundered a trade route bound for our gates. The run is destroyed. A raider who feeds on our roads unopposed will not stop at one.

variants.headline: {{gold}} gold gone with a plundered route
body: The market heard it first: a route bound for us, plundered on the road, {{gold}} gold gone with the run. What that road was worth to our towns, no tally in the capital will show.

variants.headline: Trade needs a guarded road
body: We learn that a trade route on the way to our gates has been plundered. Those who would enjoy the income of trade must also keep the road; the one cannot be had without the other. The paper wants the routes watched, and wants to know who was not watching them.

variants.headline: The road from {{origin}} is robbed
body: They say a trade route out of {{origin}}, bound for our cities, was plundered on the road. The run is ended. The loss sits at both ends, and a piece of it lands here.

variants.headline: Our outgoing trade has stopped
body: Our last outgoing trade route has ended. No trade of ours now sets out for a foreign market.

variants.headline: The last route is closed
body: It was the only outgoing trade route we still ran, and now it runs no more. With its ending, no trade of ours crosses the border. What remains is the road, and the habit of trade.

variants.headline: Every outgoing route has ended
body: Of the {{routes}} outgoing trade routes we ran, not one survives. Whatever ended them, no new route has been opened in its place. The income is gone. The paper asks who is minding the trade, and what they intend to do about it.

variants.headline: Notice to those who send trade out
body: Our outgoing trade routes have ended; we run none. Those with goods for foreign markets have, for the present, no route of ours to carry them.

variants.headline: A {{routeDistance}}-tile trade route completes its run
body: The trade route between {{ourCity}} and {{theirCity}} has completed its run: {{routeDistance}} tiles from end to end, a long road for trade by any measure.

variants.headline: Our trade reaches {{theirCity}}
body: Distance is the story: an outgoing route from {{ourCity}} has completed the {{routeDistance}}-tile run to {{theirCity}}. The farther a route reaches, the wider the market it ties to ours. Runs of this length turn a distant city into a partner of consequence, and the next one should reach farther still.

variants.headline: A long road ends at {{ourCity}}
body: Letters from the road relate that a trade route of {{routeDistance}} tiles from {{theirCity}} has completed its run to {{ourCity}}. Trade that crosses so far to reach us does more than bring income; it makes two markets one.

variants.headline: The long road to {{partner}}
body: In this season the trade road between {{ourCity}} and {{theirCity}}, {{routeDistance}} tiles apart, was run from end to end. The record notes that the way between us and {{partner}} stands open.

variants.headline: A {{routeDistance}}-tile run, completed
body: That is a lot of map between two markets. The {{ourCity}} to {{theirCity}} route just finished the full {{routeDistance}}-tile run. Both ends are the richer for it.

variants.headline: Our trade route plundered on the road
body: A trade route out of our territory has been plundered before it reached its destination. The run is lost, and with it whatever our side stood to gain.

variants.headline: {{plunderer}} takes our trade on the road
body: Our route never reached its destination. {{plunderer}} plundered it on the way, and the loss lands here at home, where the trade was to earn its keep.

variants.headline: The account of a plundered route
body: Route lost: one, outbound from our territory.
Gold taken: {{gold}}.
The entry closes against us.

variants.headline: Our route to {{destination}} is plundered
body: A trade route from our territory to {{destination}} has been plundered on the road. The run is lost. Both ends of the trade feel it, ours and {{destination}} alike.

variants.headline: Send the spears with the trade
body: One of our trade routes has been plundered on the road. Roads that make money will be robbed so long as robbery is cheap. The paper wants our trade guarded, and the robbers made to regret the road.

variants.headline: Our trade network opens
body: Our outgoing trade routes now number {{routes}}, where at the last count there were none. Our trade has begun to move beyond our own borders.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our trade goes abroad
body: Outgoing trade routes: {{routes}}, where before there were none! Our trade goes out to the world. Mark it well: our trade is on the move!

variants.headline: What an open trade network is worth
body: We ran no outgoing trade routes at the last count; we now run {{routes}}. Routes do not found themselves; someone chose to send our trade out, and the nation is the richer for the choice. The paper counts that to the government's credit.

variants.headline: The road out stands open
body: Where the road goes out, the gold comes home.

variants.headline: We plunder a foreign trade route
body: Our forces have plundered a trade route out of foreign territory. The run is at an end.

variants.headline: {{gold}} gold taken from a foreign route
body: Our forces plundered a trade route out of foreign territory and took {{gold}} gold from the run. The coin is in our treasury now; the loss sits in another ledger.

variants.headline: A route from {{origin}} to {{destination}} is plundered
body: Our forces have plundered a trade route running from {{origin}} to {{destination}}, and the run is ended on the road. The taking is effective; whether it is dignified is another question. Orderly commerce remains the more profitable habit.

variants.headline: Foreign trade turns a profit
body: Foreign trade routes, it turns out, pay well. You just have to collect in person.

variants.headline: Have we no merchants left?
body: Sir, the route our soldiers plundered set out from foreign ground, but trade is a habit between peoples, and habits break both ways. We will want open roads again one day. Robbery is a poor way to keep them.
